analysis:
All three changed files are test-only Swift code: one registration line in ClusterConsoleCheck.swift (line 64), the new ConsolePairingChangeChecks.swift, and the new ClusterServicePairingChangeTests.swift. No production source, wire protocol, key custody, attestation, or authorization logic changes in the supplied evidence.

The tests exercise cluster-service listener behavior after re-pairing, covering listener restart on a new pairing, stop on unpair, and keeping listeners on an unreadable store. They indirectly document a behavior fix whose production code is not in this batch. The fix makes the service follow a new pairing instead of leaving a stale listener key. It also asserts that the earlier pairing is refused after re-pair (handshakeRejected) and that an unsafe store (mode 0755) is a read failure, not an unpairing.

Security notes:
- Test keys are software P256 keys with a permissive verifyAttestation hook that is local to the test; it is not reachable from production code.
- The loopback test policy (.loopbackForTests) is used only in tests.
- The fixed port 45891 and pid-derived ports 46100+ are bound on loopback only in tests. This is a test flakiness risk, not a security issue.
- Fixture cleanup uses a scratch dir under the working directory and a private root.
- The tests fail closed, expecting refusal for stale pairings and for a store others may open. That is consistent with the T-053 binding and revocation intent.

The actual production change in ClusterService (ensureResponder, ensureControlResponder, ensureControl) is not supplied. Integration should confirm that it (a) fails closed on an unreadable store, (b) stops the listeners when unpaired, and (c) drops control nodes bound to an earlier local key. No finding can be made from test-only evidence. This is not a TB-007 or T-041 cache change; that definition is unrelated to these files.
